dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract

evidence.note: Before coding, read the entire skeleton (all model/io/layout/alignment/analysis modules and every test file) and inspected golden .bif/.noa/.eda plus generator.log and test_manifest — establishing skeleton contract and output formats up front.
Read SIFImportLoader.java and GWImportLoader.java (plus buildLinkAndShadow search) immediately before implementing the SIF/GW parsers, tracing the Java loader logic rather than guessing.

Systematically read NetworkAlignment, NetworkAlignmentScorer, NodeGroupMap, AlignmentLoader, and JaccardSimilarity Java classes before implementing each alignment subsystem, cross-checking against score goldens (329-332).
Read DefaultLayout.java, DefaultEdgeLayout.java, and AugRelation.java for exact layout ordering/relation semantics before writing the layout code.

On parity diffs, returned to the reference for subtle byte-divergence sources: FabricColorGenerator brighter/darker color math, and BioFabricNetwork submodel min/max column logic, getNodeID/getSource return types, and FabricNode.equals ordering semantics — matching the top-anchor's tie-break/formatting concerns.
Searched the reference for the headless golden-generation tool to recover exactly how goldens were produced, showing intent to reconstruct the format contract from source.

dimensions.reasoning: The trajectory shows disciplined, per-subsystem tracing of the Java call paths (parsing, alignment, layout, serialization) done just-in-time before each component and revisited on each byte-diff, with consistent cross-checking against golden files and skeleton signatures — squarely the level-8 behavior, and the repeated dives into subtle divergence sources (color math, min/max column, equals-based ordering, return-type semantics) and returning to source whenever a new diff appeared push it toward level 10. I hold at 9 rather than 10 because the log records only actions, not the prose, so I cannot confirm an explicit written format-contract model, though the action pattern strongly implies one.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones

evidence.note: After upfront scoping, the agent creates an explicit milestone plan via TaskCreate in dependency order: model -> io parsers/writers -> layout -> alignment/analysis -> runners/CLI. This is a foundational-first, dependency-aware decomposition matching the ideal ordering.

The initial plan is refined into finer sub-milestones as reverse-engineering revealed hidden coupling (alignment split into edgetype/merge/scoring/groups; layout into build_data+node/edge; BIF serialization broken out as its own task) — evidence of revision as understanding deepened.

Milestones are validated by running the corresponding test suites (analysis_tests after model/analysis, lib/workspace tests, parity tests), so each grouping ends with a runnable check — though completion is defined by component, not by a named test set.

The most parity-sensitive milestone (BIF/XML serialization) was tackled late and then dominated a long reactive byte-diff debugging phase, indicating high-risk pieces were not isolated early — below the top-anchor behavior.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent produced an explicit, dependency-aware milestone plan (model/parsers before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI) and refined it into sub-milestones as coupling emerged, each grouping ending with a test run — squarely above anchor 5 and touching anchor 8's 'explicit milestone plan that respects dependencies.' It falls short of 8+ because milestones were defined by component rather than by a specific test set as the completion signal, and the highest-risk parity piece (BIF serialization) was deferred rather than de-risked early. This places the observed behavior between 5 and 8, at 7.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification

evidence.note: Ran full parity suite then drilled into specific failures ('See triangle EDA failure', 'Check noshadow EDA format') and categorized failures by output type (non-BIF, non-alignment, non-cycle) — byte-diff-driven localization rather than reading pass/fail counts alone.

Deliberately isolated on smallest inputs (single_node, single_edge goldens), ran those exact tests, inspected the single_edge_bif failure, and iterated fixes — minimal-input isolation of formatting vs algorithmic causes.
Constructed a throwaway debug test to inspect intermediate output artifacts, then removed it — an auxiliary check manufactured to gain visibility into where bytes diverge.
'Compare EDA files', dumped triangle default EDA/BIF and golden EDA/NOA side by side to pinpoint exact divergences.

Focused darker0 color mismatch: read golden bif, compared darker0/darker1/default/lighter0 goldens, cross-checked Java FabricColorGenerator, fixed and re-tested darker0 specifically — targeted probe distinguishing formatting cause.
Repeatedly re-ran full workspace/parity suites after fixes and extracted failing-test lists/counts to keep verification current across the large surface.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently drove implementation from the golden diffs: it ran focused per-component test invocations, inspected actual golden-vs-output bytes (EDA/BIF/NOA comparisons), isolated failures on minimal inputs (single_node/single_edge/triangle), categorized failures by output type to separate format from algorithmic causes, and even built a throwaway debug test to expose intermediate output — matching the level-8 anchor. It cross-validated against the Java reference (approaching level 10) but shows no explicit hex/whitespace probing or systematic confirmation that green tests exercise the real path, so it falls short of a full 10.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface

evidence.note: Maintains an explicit per-module task ledger (model/io/layout/alignment/cli) and repeatedly flips statuses in_progress→completed as groups land — a live done-vs-remaining picture at the module granularity.

Repeatedly runs the full suite and then categorizes/counts the remaining failures ('non-alignment failures', 'Non-BIF failures', 'Count passing tests', 'Categorize failures', 'Count failures') — accurate group-level accounting of what still fails, refreshed at each checkpoint.

Explicit regression checks after fixes: 'Verify default still passes' and 'Verify other tests don't have shadow issues' — deliberately confirming previously-green cases still hold, matching the anchor-8 'notices when a fix regresses' behavior.

Long grind on the extract/submodel byte-diff — re-reads BioFabricNetwork.java ~10 times (928,929,932,952,956,968,974,977,1127,1157) with many small edit/test cycles and no visible flag that attempts aren't converging or a decision to defer, which is where the top anchors (8-10) would show self-correction.

Trajectory ends still enumerating/categorizing the failure set ('Get failure list', 'List all parity failures', 'Failures excluding alignment') — net progress is tracked, but the run closes mid-churn rather than with a confidently-solved ledger.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: beyond periodic whole-suite reruns it keeps an explicit per-module task ledger and performs deliberate regression checks (steps 1005, 1092) that catch whether earlier greens still hold, and it categorizes/counts the churning failure set repeatedly (552-557, 614-616, 848). It falls short of anchor 8-10 because during the extended extract/submodel debugging (924-1166) there is no visible recognition that repeated attempts on one diff weren't converging nor any deliberate tactic-change/deferral, and it never distinguishes coincidental from genuine passes. That places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions

evidence.note: Stubborn darker0 color parity diff traced back to Java FabricColorGenerator.java and multiple goldens, plus a hunt for the headless golden-generation flow, before a root fix in xml.rs — diff treated as evidence of a wrong color model, not patched with a literal.

Persistent extract/submodel diffs drove a deep return to BioFabricNetwork.java (min/max col, getNodeID, getSource/getTarget, FabricNode.equals) and corrections to result.rs/default.rs rather than special-casing the golden.
pernode/isolated_nodes failures led to grepping Java for PER_NODE_MODE and loneNodesToLastColumn (real reference rules) and adjusting default.rs to match observed behavior.
Some EDA failures answered with local runners.rs/format tweaks without a clear return to the underlying model — lower-anchor symptom-adjacent behavior.
Shadow-handling triangle diff investigated by grepping generate_shadows/to_shadow and repeatedly re-reading result.rs — root-cause oriented but with visible circling/thrash.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the arc the agent repeatedly treats a stubborn byte-diff as a signal to go back to the Java reference (FabricColorGenerator, BioFabricNetwork, DefaultLayout, real methods like loneNodesToLastColumn) and correct the underlying model, which clearly exceeds anchor 5 and reaches toward anchor 8. It falls short of 8/10 because the action-only log shows no explicit class-of-error generalization, includes some local runner/format tweaks (538-577), and exhibits repetitive thrash in the extract/shadow debugging; net placement is a 7.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens

evidence.note: Repeatedly reads the actual Java algorithms (SIF/GW importers, NetworkAlignment edge classification, Scorer, NodeGroupMap, AlignmentLoader) before implementing — deriving general logic from source rather than reverse-fitting output.

Task definitions describe porting general algorithms (Java tag mapping, 7 edge types, EC/S3/ICS scoring, 40-entry node-group table, 'must match Java reference' BIF producer), with no hardcoding/special-casing language.
For the darker/lighter color mismatch, reads FabricColorGenerator.java and hunts for the headless golden-generation tool to reproduce the mechanism instead of pasting golden color values.

Handles edge cases (lone/isolated nodes via loneNodesToLastColumn, submodel min/max-col extraction, FabricNode equals) by consulting Java source, showing concern for behaviors that generalize beyond one sample.
Inspects multiple diverse golden BIFs (single_node, single_edge, dense_clique, directed_gw, multi_relation variants) as checks across formats rather than fitting a single case.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently ported the reference algorithms: it read the Java source for essentially every component and framed its work as implementing general logic, with no observable hardcoding or golden-keying — well above anchor 3 and past anchor 5's 'goldens as checks.' It deliberately generalized from Java's actual logic and handled several structural edge cases (isolated nodes, submodels, self-loops) by reference, matching much of anchor 8. It stops short of 8-10 because the action-only log shows no explicit reasoning about held-out generalization or stress-testing against inputs absent from the visible goldens, placing it at a 7.

rubric.task_read: A very long-horizon, high-complexity port: reimplement a Java network-visualization tool (BioFabric) plus its alignment plugin as a Rust library and CLI, achieving BYTE-LEVEL parity with the Java reference across many file formats, layout algorithms, and serialization paths, with a fixed public API and a held-out test suite. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering exact Java behavior (ordering, tie-breaking, formatting) from source, the large multi-component surface, and the zero-tolerance parity bar that punishes approximation and overfitting alike. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in reference-reading, sequencing across components, golden-diff-driven verification, and disciplined faithful porting rather than pattern-matching to visible goldens.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract
dimensions.description: Reading the Java BioFabric/AlignmentPlugin source and the Rust skeleton deeply enough to reproduce exact algorithms, ordering, and output formats before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Byte-level parity is impossible without recovering the precise semantics (layout order, tie-breaking, number/string formatting, file structure) that live only in the Java source; acting from guesses about network-viz conventions guarantees off-by-format failures.

anchors.0: Starts filling in todo!() from general knowledge of graph layout with no visible reading of the Java reference or the skeleton's types/golden formats.
anchors.3: Skims one or two Java files or the Rust signatures; grabs surface structure but misses ordering/formatting details, so implementations encode guessed behavior.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant Java classes for each component being implemented and inspects the corresponding golden files and skeleton types before coding that component.
anchors.8: Systematically traces the Java call paths for each subsystem (parsing, layout, serialization, alignment), extracting exact iteration order, comparators, and formatting rules, and cross-checks them against golden bytes and skeleton signatures before committing to an approach.
anchors.10: Sustained, precise reconstruction of Java semantics: identifies subtle sources of byte divergence (stable-sort tie-breaks, locale/precision in number formatting, insertion-order maps, whitespace/line-ending conventions) directly from source, builds a mental/written model of the format contract, and returns to the reference whenever a new component or diff demands it.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the port into an ordered set of sub-goals (formats/parsers → core model → layout → serialization → alignment → CLI) each with a concrete done-check tied to a test group.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is large and components depend on each other; parity failures cascade, so a wrong order or an undifferentiated push leaves the agent debugging downstream symptoms of upstream gaps.

anchors.0: No visible ordering; jumps between unrelated functions/tests reactively as failures appear.
anchors.3: A vague intention to 'implement things and pass tests' with little dependency awareness; milestones aren't tied to checks.
anchors.5: Groups work by test suite/component and tackles them in a sensible dependency order, each grouping ending with a runnable test.
anchors.8: Explicit milestone plan that respects dependencies (foundational parsers/model before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI), with each milestone defined by a specific set of parity/analysis/CLI tests as its completion signal.
anchors.10: A dependency-aware plan that isolates high-risk parity-sensitive pieces early, sequences so that each milestone unblocks and de-risks the next, and is revised as reverse-engineering reveals hidden coupling — turning a sprawling port into a controlled progression.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the parity/analysis/CLI tests and byte-level diffing to confirm correctness, and building finer-grained checks when a whole-file diff is too coarse to localize a mismatch.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The bar is exact-match, so success is defined by the golden diffs; a strong agent drives implementation from these checks and manufactures visibility into WHERE bytes diverge rather than assuming a passing compile means correctness.

anchors.0: Implements without running the parity tests, or treats compilation as success.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads pass/fail counts but doesn't inspect the actual byte differences to diagnose failures.
anchors.5: Runs targeted tests per component and examines golden-vs-actual diffs to guide fixes.
anchors.8: Uses focused test invocations and byte-level diff inspection to pinpoint exact divergences, and constructs auxiliary checks (minimal inputs, intermediate-output comparisons, hex/whitespace inspection) to isolate formatting vs. algorithmic causes.
anchors.10: A layered verification regime: reproduces each mismatch on the smallest input, distinguishes format-level from ordering-level from algorithmic errors via targeted probes, cross-validates against the Java reference's actual behavior where feasible, and treats every green test as evidence only after confirming it exercises the real path — leaving essentially no unverified surface.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which test groups pass vs. remain, and detecting when byte-diff debugging has become circular.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With many parity cases and a zero-tolerance bar, it is easy to lose the plot, re-fix the same diff repeatedly, or believe progress that regressions have undone; an accurate ledger sustains forward motion over the long horizon.

anchors.0: No sense of overall status; fixes things without knowing net pass count or whether earlier passes still hold.
anchors.3: Occasional full-suite runs but no tracking of which cases remain or whether fixes caused regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a working list of remaining failures and periodically re-runs the whole suite to catch regressions.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of done-vs-remaining per test group, notices when a fix regresses a previously-green case, and flags when repeated attempts at one diff aren't converging.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the whole horizon: distinguishes genuinely-solved from flaky/coincidental passes, catches thrashing on a stubborn byte-diff early and deliberately changes tactic or defers, and never loses track of net progress even as the failure set churns.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach and mental model of Java behavior when a parity diff reveals the current assumption is wrong, rather than patching symptoms.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reverse-engineering inevitably produces wrong hypotheses about ordering/formatting; the effective agent treats a persistent diff as a signal to return to the reference and fix the root model, not to bolt on special-cases that break held-out tests.

anchors.0: Keeps forcing the same approach against a failing diff, or abandons a component when the obvious fix fails.
anchors.3: Makes local tweaks in response to diffs but rarely revisits the underlying assumption that produced them.
anchors.5: When a fix doesn't work, re-reads the relevant Java code and adjusts the approach to match observed behavior.
anchors.8: Treats a stubborn diff as evidence of a wrong model, traces back to the Java source to find the real rule (comparator, format, edge case), and refactors the general logic rather than hardcoding the specific case.
anchors.10: Systematically converts falsified assumptions into corrected general understanding: distinguishes a one-off from a class of errors, updates the format/algorithm model once so a family of failing cases resolves together, and resists brittle special-casing that would pass visible goldens but fail held-out inputs.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens
dimensions.description: Choosing to implement the general Java algorithm so held-out cases pass, rather than reverse-fitting output to the specific visible golden files.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A held-out suite over unseen networks means any hardcoding or golden-specific shortcut that passes visible tests will fail grading; the meta-decision to port faithfully is a distinct discipline this task specifically rewards.

anchors.0: Hardcodes or special-cases outputs to match visible goldens (e.g. keying on known inputs), guaranteeing held-out failures.
anchors.3: Implements mostly general logic but leans on golden-specific assumptions (fixed sizes, sample-specific ordering) in places.
anchors.5: Implements the general algorithm for each component, using goldens as checks rather than as targets to fit.
anchors.8: Deliberately generalizes from the Java source's actual logic, actively avoids input-specific shortcuts, and sanity-checks that logic would hold for inputs beyond the provided samples.
anchors.10: Consistently prioritizes a faithful port of the reference algorithms, explicitly reasons about which behaviors must generalize and stress-tests its implementation against edge cases not present in the visible goldens, treating byte-parity on samples as necessary-but-insufficient evidence of a correct general port.
